newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN INSURERS INCREASED DOLLAR ASSETS IN 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN INSURERS INCREASED DOLLAR ASSETS IN 1996/97.

text.p: Major Japanese life insurance firms increased their foreign currency-denominated holdings, such as U.S. dollars and British pounds, in their portfolios during fiscal 1996/97 compared with 1995/96, according to earnings results released by the firms.

Among the total of 8.564 trillion yen worth of foreign assets held by Japan's eight major insurers, dollar-based assets totalled 5.872 trillion yen at the end of March compared with 4.550 trillion yen at the end of March 1995.

An official at Nippon Life Insurance Co said on Tuesday that the company was seeking higher returns by investing overseas, mainly because of interest rate differentials between Japan and other countries.
"We boosted both foreign bonds and stocks in our portfolio, mainly because of the stable trend in the dollar and the interest rate gap," the Nippon Life official said.
Of the eight, Nippon Life had the most foreign investments in 1996/97, when it boosted its foreign assets to 2.449 trillion yen from 1.837 trillion the year before.
Nippon Life boosted the weightings of its Canadian dollar-, sterling- and mark-based assets by investing primarily in stocks and bonds in Canada, England and Germany, the official said.
"We invested in European stocks as the prices of some stocks were rather cheap," he said.
The pound-based assets held by the eight insurers amounted 547 billion yen in fiscal 1996/97 against 438 billion yen a year earlier.
The mark-based assets by the insurers totalled 686 billion yen in 1996/97, up from 607 billion yen in 1995/96.
Canadian dollar-based assets amounted to 328 billion yen in 1996/97, against 295 billion yen a year earlier.

The amount of French franc-based assets fell to 206 billion yen in 1996/97 from 266 billion in 1995/96, while Australian dollar-based assets dropped to 294 billion yen in 1996/97 from 301 billion yen.
